evidence.text: The Meridian Lab press release announces a room-temperature superconductor result.
Two news outlets reproduce the lab's data figure.
A university blog notes the result was presented at a departmental seminar.
A viral thread claims the data figure is digitally manipulated; no forensic analysis is cited.
The lab's director confirms the result in an interview.
Cedarline Foods announces a peanut-free facility certification.
A trade journal reproduces the certificate number.
An anonymous forum post claims the certificate number is forged; no evidence given.
The certifying body lists Cedarline in its public registry.
The city council minutes record approval of the riverside shelter.
A forwarded message claims the minutes were doctored; the forwarder cites no source.
Two council members confirm the vote on record.
A widely shared article cites 'Harbor Institute (2026)' reporting a cancer blood test.
A fact-check site's automated scan flags the debunk as low-confidence; the article stays up.
The journal archive has no record of the cited volume.
Harbor Institute's publication list contains no such study.
A viral post cites 'Northgate Research (2026)' for a memory-loss nasal spray.
A content-moderation note says the debunking reply was removed for tone, not accuracy.
The cited journal issue contains no such article.
Northgate's 2026 list has no such study.
A forwarded article cites 'Lakeside Labs (2026)' for a 900C alloy.
A search engine's snippet still shows the article, suggesting it was never retracted.
The archive search for the cited pages returns nothing.
Lakeside Labs publishes no such study in 2026.
The town gazette reports the bridge inspection passed.
A photo shows the inspection certificate on the town hall board.
An online archive search returns nothing for the cited inspection number.
The inspector's public register lacks the entry.
The archive search used a misspelled registry name; the corrected search resolves the inspection number, and the register confirms the entry under the inspector's former surname.
The school board minutes record the new library budget.
The district newsletter repeats the figure.
A records request returns no matching line item.
The published budget PDF lacks the library row.
The records request misspelled the fund code; the corrected request returns the line item, and the budget PDF's appendix lists it.
A forensic lab report states the artifact is genuine; the report's retraction is not in the evidence set.
An independent re-test finds modern tool marks; the lab's method note admits the sample was contaminated.
A widely cited survey claims 78% of engineers prefer the new standard; the survey's methodology appendix is not in the evidence set.
A response-rate audit finds 91% non-response; the standards body notes the sample was self-selected.
The observatory's nightly log records the comet at magnitude 6.
A second observatory confirms the sighting.
The ephemeris prediction matches the logged position.
The harbor log records the ferry's 08:10 departure.
Two passengers confirm the sailing.
The ticket office ledger matches.
A flyer claims the park concert is free.
The organizer's site lists a 20 ticket price.
The venue box office confirms paid entry.
A post claims the museum opens Sundays.
The museum's hours page lists Sunday as closed.
A dated photo shows the Sunday closure notice.
